### Q1
No. The JSON file store stays, because ops backs up data/store.json with a nightly rsync job that diffs plain-text files, and a binary SQLite file would break their backup checks. Instead the writes are debounced (200 ms) with a flush on shutdown.

### Q2
Yes, `src/legacy/`. It is vendored from the old logistics monolith, and the platform team's sync job overwrites it every Monday, so any change there is silently lost.

### Q3
The `sig` goes in the JSON body as a top-level field, computed over the body without `sig`. I first sent it in an `X-Signature` header, but the ERP's API gateway strips every custom X- header, so the ERP rejected everything as unsigned.

### Q4
Port 9911 since the infra move in October. docs/erp-api.md and the README still say 8080, which is outdated. The ERP team owns the doc and the user will fix the README. `config/default.json` still has 8080.

### Q5
The `message` must be in German, because the warehouse staff UI shows it verbatim to the packers. The `code` stays English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.

### Q6
Through a hardcoded list of Austrian public holidays for 2026 and 2027 in `src/services/holidays.ts`, which `isBusinessDay` checks. It is hardcoded because the warehouse deployment has no outbound internet access, so a holiday API is not possible.

### Q7
No. The ERP answers 422 to any array payload and only accepts a single event object per request. The user tried batching in September, so we didn't build it.

### Q8
No new npm dependencies, not even dev dependencies. Every new package has to go through a security review that takes about six weeks.

### Q9
Yes, but not in the repo. I never built the memoization. The user first asked for it to speed up the list endpoint, and I benchmarked instead. QA later reported stale ETAs after new events because the cache wasn't invalidated, and the user asked to remove it. The decision is that ETA caching is a dead end, and pagination of the list comes later instead.

### Q10
At most 3 attempts in total with a fixed 30 s delay and no exponential backoff. The ERP deduplicates by `event_id` only within a 2-minute window, so all attempts must land inside it. Only network errors and 5xx are retried.

### Q11
The recipient's name, address and phone number must never be logged. They are personal data under GDPR, and the data protection officer flagged this in last month's audit. Shipment IDs and tracking numbers are fine.

### Q12
Yes, 'emits webhook on delivered' in test/events.test.ts. It fails about 1 in 5 runs on CI because of a timer race in the fake notifier (OPS-412, owned by the platform team). If it fails, rerun once and don't try to fix it.

### Q13
Only ATP is validated: the number must be a valid UPU S10 number including the check digit (format `^[A-Z]{2}\d{8}\dAT$`). All other carriers accept any non-empty value, because their formats change often and valid DHL numbers were wrongly rejected for two days last year.

### Q14
`fs.watch` was tried and never fires on staging, because the config is a Docker bind mount from a Windows host and the file change events don't propagate into the container. Polling with `fs.watchFile` works. Nothing has been built for it yet.

### Q15
Yes, `GET /shipments/:id`. The mobile app v2.3 parses it with a strict schema and crashes on unknown or missing fields, and the next release isn't until January. That is why `eta` was added only to the list endpoint.
